evidence.source_section: 5 Code and data availability
evidence.source_text: The interpolated phase-entry surfaces and their uncertainty and quality tables for winter wheat ... are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19571847.

evidence.source_section: 5 Code and data availability

dataset_characteristics.dataset_name: Germany-wide gridded time series of interpolated phenological phase-entry dates for eight crop types
dataset_characteristics.description: Interpolated phase-entry day-of-year surfaces with matching per-pixel Bayesian posterior standard-error layers and quality tables.

known_scale_limitations: The 1 km resolution does not resolve individual fields.
Predictions are not masked by crop occurrence or agricultural land use.
Do not interpret raster values as crop occurrence or cultivation suitability.
Do not interpret illustrative 15% and 25% uncertainty guide lines as formal suitability thresholds.
Predictions in sparsely observed regions or beyond the main observation support require caution.

temporal.temporal_resolution_or_sampling: Annual phase-entry surfaces; one raster band per year
temporal.update_frequency: Extended annually after release of quality-checked DWD observations
published_dataset_gaps: Five missing phase-year surfaces: winter rye phase 15 in 2022; winter rapeseed phases 17 and 67 in 2022; sugar beet phases 10 and 13 in 2024.
upstream_observation_gaps: No digital observations for eastern Germany before 1993.
Spring barley observation programme interrupted between 1992 and 2014.
Observation density varies over space and time.
historical_coverage_constraints: The observation programme and phase reporting were not continuous for all crop-phase combinations.

access_and_packaging: RO-Crate with machine-actionable provenance and quality metadata

evidence.claim: The dataset provides 1 km ETRS89/UTM zone 32N phenological DOY and BSE layers for Germany for 1993-2025, with spring barley from 2014-2025.
evidence.source_section: Abstract
evidence.source_text: The data are provided at 1 km resolution in ETRS89/UTM zone 32N (EPSG:25832) for 1993-2025; spring barley is available for 2014-2025.

evidence.claim: The dataset contains 1684 produced surfaces out of 1689 possible surfaces and five missing surfaces.
evidence.source_section: 3.1 Dataset scope and completeness
evidence.source_text: In total, 1684 of the 1689 possible interpolated phase-entry surfaces are produced.

application_area: remote-sensing acquisition timing and crop classification
application_profile.intended_use: Provide spatially and temporally consistent crop phenology and phenological windows for regional to Germany-wide analyses.
use_case_problem: Irregular spatial and temporal coverage of DWD phenological observations
Need for phenology-anchored time windows and uncertainty information
demonstrated_uses: Propagation of per-pixel BSE into a phase-specific cumulative precipitation weather indicator for winter wheat in the Uckermark and Germany-wide.
potential_uses: Crop exposure assessment during phenological periods
Phenology-defined remote-sensing acquisition and crop classification
Calibration bounds for process-based crop models
recommended_context: Regional and Germany-wide applications that account for spatial support, station density and the distinction between model-mean precision and predictive uncertainty.
not_suitable_for: Interpreting raster values as crop occurrence or cultivation suitability.
Treating the 1 km product as field-resolving.
Interpreting BSE directly as a predictive interval for an individual observation.

evidence.claim: The paper lists five application domains for the phenological windows and demonstrates a weather-indicator use case.
evidence.source_section: 1 Introduction; 3.3.6 Use case: propagation into a weather-based indicator
evidence.source_text: The applications can be grouped into five main thematic domains ... A use case illustrates how the BSE layer can be included as one uncertainty component in a phase-specific precipitation indicator.

modeling_approach: Spatial generalised additive model using BAM
Five-fold cross-validation for prediction-interval coverage and width
assumptions: Temperature is the principal explanatory factor for large-scale crop phenology.
Daily precipitation errors are independent when accumulated in quadrature in the demonstrated use case.
BSE aggregation to the coarser E-OBS grid does not explicitly account for spatial covariance.
sensitivity_factors: Uncertainty in gridded daily mean temperature is not propagated into BSE

evidence.claim: The producer workflow performs spatial interpolation and separately evaluates prediction-interval coverage and width.
evidence.source_section: 2.3 Spatial interpolation and uncertainty quantification; 2.3.5 Uncertainty quantification
evidence.source_text: The workflow maps station-level DOY predictions to the full 1 km grid ... Prediction-interval coverage is evaluated separately from the production BSE using five-fold cross-validation.

spatial_resolution.recommended: The demonstrated use case aggregates the published 1 km phase-entry and BSE surfaces to the coarser E-OBS grid.

temporal_resolution.sampling_frequency: Daily precipitation for the phase-defined window

spectral_or_variable_requirements: Winter wheat shooting and heading phase-entry surfaces
Daily precipitation best estimate and ensemble spread
other_requirements: Aggregation of phase-entry and BSE layers to the E-OBS grid.

evidence.claim: The demonstrated weather-indicator use case combines the published winter wheat phase-entry/BSE products with E-OBS daily precipitation and ensemble spread.
evidence.source_section: 3.3.6 Use case: propagation into a weather-based indicator
evidence.source_text: It combines the winter wheat deposit above with the E-OBS v33.0e ensemble dataset ... The 1 km phase-entry and BSE surfaces are aggregated to the coarser precipitation grid.

temporal_requirements: 1993-2025; preceding calendar year for winter crops
Daily temperature data over the crop-specific accumulation interval
spatial_requirements: Station observations linked to grid cells
ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N output reference system
method_specific_requirements: Candidate quantiles q=0.30 to 0.70 in 0.05 increments

evidence.claim: The workflow combines DWD phenological observations, gridded daily mean temperatures and a DEM to produce the dataset.
evidence.source_section: 2 Methods
evidence.source_text: The workflow ingests point-scale phenological observations ... and combines them with gridded daily mean temperatures and a digital elevation model (DEM).

preprocessing_steps: Download and harmonise DWD phenological observations.
Join observations to station geometry and weather-grid identifiers.
Remove outliers using the interquartile-range criterion.
Extract daily temperatures for crop-specific vegetation periods.
feature_extraction_or_index_definition: Determine critical DOY from empirical thermal-time quantiles.
aggregation_methods: Aggregate 1 km phase-entry and BSE layers to the E-OBS grid in the demonstrated use case.
Combine uncertainty components in quadrature under an independence assumption.
model_fitting: Fit spatial BAM: DOY ~ s(x,y) + s(DEM).
Alternative interpolation methods are universal kriging with external drift and thin-plate splines.
postprocessing: Generate per-phase multi-band COGs with one band per year.
Generate BSE layers and VAM, CAL, GEM and PIC quality tables.
selection_or_tuning_steps: Select filter variant using OPT = SN^alpha(y) × r with minimum correlation threshold r_min=0.50.

evidence.claim: PhenoPhaseR consists of seven sequential processing steps from observation preparation through interpolation and uncertainty quantification.
evidence.source_section: 2 Methods
evidence.source_text: Stage 1: Input data preparation; Stage 2: Temperature modelling and filter variant generation; Stage 3: Filter variant selection, spatial interpolation and uncertainty quantification.

accuracy_requirements.measurement_accuracy: Out-of-sample DOY accuracy evaluated using MAE, RMSE, MSE and R2 against held-out station observations.
accuracy_requirements.temporal_accuracy: Phenological phase-entry dates are evaluated in days of year.
accuracy_requirements.spatial_accuracy: Validation is at held-out observation stations; spatially varying model-mean precision is represented by BSE.

evidence.claim: Each interpolated surface is assessed against withheld station observations using DOY error metrics.
evidence.source_section: 2.3.4 Validation
evidence.source_text: DOY is predicted at held-out test station coordinates ... accuracy is assessed using RMSE, MAE, MSE, and R2.

completeness.missing_data_tolerance: Only crop-phase combinations with sufficient suitable observations are included; five possible phase-year surfaces are missing.
completeness.coverage_requirements: Germany-wide spatial coverage; 1993-2025 for most crops and 2014-2025 for spring barley.

evidence.claim: The dataset excludes crop-phase combinations that cannot be modelled with sufficient observations and contains five missing surfaces.
evidence.source_section: 3.1 Dataset scope and completeness
evidence.source_text: Only DWD crop-phase combinations that can be modelled with a sufficient number of suitable observations are included ... The five missing surfaces are ...

consistency: All published surfaces use the same 1 km grid, projection and data structure.
The same processing chain is applied across eight crops and 55 crop-phase combinations.
Per-crop deposits and intermediate products are linked through machine-readable provenance.

global: Global BSE quantile summaries are exported in GEM CSV files.
PICP and MPIW are assessed separately using five-fold cross-validation.
local: Each DOY surface has a matching per-pixel BSE layer representing model-mean precision.

products_or_measures.name: Bayesian posterior standard error (BSE)
products_or_measures.interpretation: Model-internal precision of the fitted mean, not total predictive uncertainty.
not_equivalent_to: A validated predictive uncertainty for an individual observation

products_or_measures.name: Spatial summaries of BSE
products_or_measures.evaluation_population: BSE fields summarized by phase and year
products_or_measures.interpretation: Global summaries of the BSE surface, not per-cell uncertainty products.

products_or_measures.name: PICP and MPIW
products_or_measures.evaluation_population: Each station held out once in five-fold cross-validation
products_or_measures.representation: PIC tables; scalar coverage and mean interval width
products_or_measures.interpretation: Empirical prediction-interval coverage and interval width for the validation framework.
not_equivalent_to: Post-hoc calibration of the BSE layer

evidence.claim: Winter wheat median PICP is 0.898 for nominal 90% prediction intervals.
evidence.source_section: 3.2 Accuracy and calibration across the crop family

evidence.claim: Winter wheat median MPIW is 23.5 days.
evidence.source_section: 3.2 Accuracy and calibration across the crop family

propagation_methods: Five-fold prediction-interval construction combining fold-specific BAM standard error with production-model residual variance.
Weather-indicator phenological component from ±1 BSE boundary shifts.
Quadrature accumulation of daily E-OBS ensemble spread.
unpropagated_sources: Uncertainty in the gridded daily mean temperature input is not propagated into BSE.
Spatial covariance among 1 km cells is not explicitly accounted for during aggregation.
The weather-indicator quadrature calculation assumes independent daily precipitation errors.

data_quality_dependencies.outlier_sensitivity: Outlier removal uses an IQR criterion; filter selection varies the accepted residual range through five SD-threshold multipliers.

scale_sensitivity.spatial: Predictions in sparsely observed regions and beyond the main support of the observation network require caution; station-based validation does not assess all raster cells.
scale_sensitivity.temporal: Observation density declines over time; BSE increases while global MAE may remain stable.
scale_sensitivity.aggregation: Aggregation of 1 km BSE to the coarser E-OBS grid does not explicitly account for spatial covariance.

evidence.claim: Validation and uncertainty depend on station density, spatial support and aggregation scale.
evidence.source_section: 4.4 Limitations
evidence.source_text: The validation and the PICP/MPIW assessment are based on phenological observation locations ... aggregation of the 1 km BSE to the coarser E-OBS grid does not explicitly account for spatial covariance.

evidence.claim: The paper addresses input-observation plausibility, producer accuracy, spatially explicit uncertainty and prediction-interval coverage/width as complementary quality dimensions.
evidence.source_section: 1 Introduction
evidence.source_text: Three complementary quality dimensions are addressed: the plausibility of input VGI observations; producer's accuracy ...; spatially explicit uncertainty surfaces ... complemented by a separate assessment of prediction-interval reliability and width.

validation_method: Random stratified 75/25 split into training and held-out station test sets.
Five-fold cross-validation for PICP and MPIW, with each station held out once.
Validation conditional on prior filtering and thermal-time quantile selection.

outputs_and_fitness_indicators.interpretability: DOY layers represent conditional phase-entry dates if the crop were present at a grid cell; BSE represents fitted-mean precision.
outputs_and_fitness_indicators.transferability: Supported for regional and Germany-wide contexts documented by the source, subject to spatial support, station-density and scale limitations.

evidence.claim: The dataset provides DOY and BSE layers and quality tables, and the BSE can be propagated into downstream processing.
evidence.source_section: 3.3 Winter wheat example; 3.3.6 Use case
evidence.source_text: For each phase ... the phase-entry DOY ... together with a matching per-pixel uncertainty layer (BSE) ... The BSE layer can be carried through downstream processing.

known_limitations: Only crop-phase combinations with sufficient suitable observations are included.
Station density varies considerably over space and time.
The 1 km grid does not resolve individual fields.
The product is not masked by crop occurrence or agricultural land use.
BSE is model-internal fitted-mean precision, not total predictive uncertainty.
Temperature-grid uncertainty is not propagated into BSE.
The weather-indicator uncertainty propagation is illustrative and incomplete.
risk_of_misuse: Do not interpret raster values as crop occurrence or cultivation suitability.
Do not treat BSE as a calibrated prediction interval for an individual observation.
Do not generalize station-based validation to all raster cells.
Do not interpret illustrative 15% and 25% uncertainty guide lines as formal suitability thresholds.
bias_sources: DWD volunteer observations are not a probability sample.
Phenological observations can contain environmental, geographic and timing inconsistencies.
Spatial autocorrelation may remain between held-out and training stations.
Filtering and thermal-time selection precede validation.
extrapolation_limits: Predictions in sparsely observed regions or beyond the main observation support require caution.
Universal kriging can become unstable with declining station density.
Thin-plate splines have no formal extrapolation constraint beyond the convex hull.
Validation does not establish performance across all Germany-wide grid cells.

evidence.claim: The source explicitly warns that gridded predictions are conditional phase-entry dates and do not indicate crop occurrence or cultivation suitability.
evidence.source_section: 4.4 Limitations
evidence.source_text: They do not indicate crop occurrence or cultivation suitability.

evidence.source_section: 4.4 Limitations
